title: Port severe weather playbook
action: Hold new bookings at the exposed port, move critical SKUs to alternate sailings, and pre-clear customs at the receiving DC.
expected_effect: Cuts delay exposure by 20-35 percent for urgent SKUs.

title: Labor disruption playbook
action: Reroute high-margin SKUs through the nearest non-strike port and reserve spot capacity with the secondary carrier.
expected_effect: Reduces stockout probability when the disruption lasts longer than five days.

title: Congestion and freight spike playbook
action: Split shipments across two lanes, expedite the top revenue SKUs, and defer low-margin replenishment until rates normalize.
expected_effect: Protects service level while limiting emergency freight spend.

title: Trade-policy shock playbook
action: Check tariff exposure, move purchase orders to qualified exempt suppliers, and reserve inventory for contracted customers first.
expected_effect: Contains margin loss and keeps customer-critical orders moving.

title: Input shortage playbook
action: Lock remaining raw material allocation, approve substitute ingredients, and run demand shaping for low-priority SKUs.
expected_effect: Preserves production continuity for strategic products.

title: Demand spike playbook
action: Raise near-term safety stock, increase pack-out shifts, and prioritize channels with the highest contribution margin.
expected_effect: Improves fill rate during a sudden demand surge.

title: Supplier quality failure playbook
action: Quarantine affected lots, switch open orders to the alternate supplier, and increase inbound inspection sampling for the next three receipts.
expected_effect: Avoids downstream recalls and protects customer shipments.
